Findings

HIGHF1INPUT accepts new connections to any portPolicy −15

No rule refuses them, and the policy of filter/INPUT is ACCEPT. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.

Fix

Add rules for the traffic that is needed and test them, with a way back, then set the policy to DROP. The recommended baseline (--baseline) is a complete rule set to start from.
  1. Deny by default (IPv4)
    iptables -P INPUT DROP
HIGHF24 services are open to any source because INPUT accepts by defaultExposure −14

No rule names their ports: A service on 8472/udp; sshd on 22/tcp; kubelet on 10250/tcp; kube-proxy on 10256/tcp. Close the default first; then accept each port that must stay reachable, for its clients only.

HIGHF3FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule namesPolicy −10

No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. The rules show that this host routes packets (address translation or Docker), so other hosts can send traffic through it to every network it reaches, including container and virtual networks.

Fix

Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.
  1. Deny forwarding by default (IPv4)
    iptables -P FORWARD DROP

Fix

kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster. To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which sees the packet before the translation. The command below is for port 30080/tcp. For each of the other ports (30443/tcp), run it again with its protocol and its port.
  1. Drop port 30080 for all but the known clients, in front of the translation
    iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -p tcp -m tcp --dport 30080 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP

Fix

kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster. To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which sees the packet before the translation.

Recommended baseline

A complete rule set to start from, made for this host. It is not what the report measures the loaded rules against. Read it before use: iptables-restore replaces the rules that are loaded. The same text comes from iptables-analyzer --baseline.

IPv4, for iptables-restore
# Recommended IPv4 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (iptables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound traffic; outbound traffic is allowed. FORWARD keeps its
# policy: this host routes packets by rules that this file does not replace.
# Apply with "iptables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p icmp -m icmp --icmp-type 8 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Jumps of the present INPUT chain to chains that other programs manage.
# They are repeated here because INPUT is flushed. A chain that accepts
# traffic decides before the rules below: review what each one admits.
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m comment --comment "kubernetes load balancer firewall" -j KUBE-PROXY-FIREWALL
-A INPUT -m comment --comment "kubernetes health check service ports" -j KUBE-NODEPORTS
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m comment --comment "kubernetes externally-visible service portals" -j KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES
-A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Other listening services found on this host. Uncomment only what must be
# reachable, preferably with -s <trusted-cidr>:
# -A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 8472 -j ACCEPT   # unknown process
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10250 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kubelet
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10256 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kube-proxy
COMMIT
IPv6, for ip6tables-restore
# Recommended IPv6 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (ip6tables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "ip6tables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Neighbor discovery is untracked by conntrack and must be allowed explicitly;
# a hop limit of 255 proves the sender is on-link.
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 134 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "router advertisement (SLAAC)" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 135 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor solicitation" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 136 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor advertisement" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 130 -m comment --comment "multicast listener query" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -d fe80::/10 -p udp -m udp --sport 547 --dport 546 -m comment --comment "DHCPv6 client" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s ::1/128 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 128 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh6-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Other listening services found on this host. Uncomment only what must be
# reachable, preferably with -s <trusted-cidr>:
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10250 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kubelet
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10256 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kube-proxy
COMMIT
  • SSH stays reachable on TCP port 22 (detected from the listening sshd).
  • Both families are always generated: IPv6 gets addresses automatically (SLAAC), so an unused stack must be closed too.
  • Keep a second SSH session open and apply with an automatic rollback, for example:
  • printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec iptables-restore --noflush /root/baseline.v4\n' > /root/apply.v4 && chmod +x /root/apply.v4 && iptables-apply -t 60 -c /root/apply.v4
  • printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec ip6tables-restore --noflush /root/baseline.v6\n' > /root/apply.v6 && chmod +x /root/apply.v6 && ip6tables-apply -t 60 -c /root/apply.v6
  • Persist the result with your distribution's mechanism (e.g. iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4 with iptables-persistent).
  • The baseline keeps the jumps of INPUT to chains of other programs (KUBE-PROXY-FIREWALL, KUBE-NODEPORTS, KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES, KUBE-FIREWALL). Rules in those chains are not part of the baseline: a chain that accepts traffic opens it whatever the baseline says.
  • IPv4 FORWARD keeps its policy (ACCEPT): this host routes packets, and the baseline does not replace its forwarding rules.
